The '''Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant''' 
({{lang-bn|রূপপুর পারমাণবিক বিদ্যুৎকেন্দ্র}}) will be a 2.4 [[GWe|GW<sub>e</sub>]] nuclear power plant in [[Bangladesh]]. The nuclear power plant is being constructed at Rooppur of [[Ishwardi]] upazila in [[Pabna District]], on the bank of the river [[Padma]], {{convert|87|mi}} west of [[Dhaka]]. It will be the country's first [[nuclear power plant]], and the first of the two units is expected to go into operation in 2024.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2015/05/04/cabinet-clears-draft-law-to-form-company-to-operate-rooppur-nuclear-power-plant |title=Cabinet clears draft law to form company to operate Rooppur nuclear power plant |work=bdnews24.com |date=4 May 2015 |access-date=6 June 2015}}</ref><ref name=wnn-20151020/><ref>{{citation |url=http://www.thefinancialexpress-bd.com/2015/12/25/7510 |title=Rooppur nuclear deal signed with Russia |work=The Financial Express |location=Dhaka |date=25 December 2015 |access-date=27 December 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151226124208/http://www.thefinancialexpress-bd.com/2015/12/25/7510 |archive-date=26 December 2015}}</ref> The [[VVER|VVER-1200/523]] [[Nuclear reactor]] and critical infrastructures are being built by the [[Russia]]n [[Rosatom|Rosatom State Atomic Energy Corporation]].<ref name="rosatom.ru">{{cite web |title=RPV welded for unit 1 of Bangladesh nuclear power plant
|url=https://www.rosatom.ru/en/press-centre/industry-in-media/rpv-welded-for-unit-1-of-bangladesh-nuclear-power-plant/|website=Rosatom|access-date=15 May 2020}}</ref> In the main construction period, the total number of employees will reach 12,500, including 2,500 specialists from [[Russia]]. It is expected to generate around 15% of the country's electricity when completed.

==History==

=== Planning ===

The plan to establish a nuclear power plant in the then East Pakistan was made in 1961.<ref name=WNA>{{citation |url=http://www.world-nuclear.org/info/Country-Profiles/Countries-A-F/Bangladesh/ |title=Nuclear Power in Bangladesh |website=World Nuclear Association |access-date=1 January 2016}}</ref> In 1963, the Rooppur village of the Pabna district was selected for the proposed plant and {{convert|254|acre|ha}} of land was acquired. The plan was to establish a 200MW nuclear power plant in the selected site. Discussions took place with the Government of Canada from 1964 to 1966. Discussions with the governments of Sweden and Norway were also going on in those years. However, no real progress was made. In 1970, the project was scrapped.

After the [[independence of Bangladesh]], the Government of [[Bangladesh]] started discussion with the [[Soviet Union]] in 1974, but no agreement was reached. In 1976–77, the French company ''Sofratom'' conducted a feasibility study and found the project at Rooppur feasible. In 1980, a 125 MW nuclear power plant project was approved. However, this effort also did not materialize. In the 1987-88 period, another feasibility study was conducted and the decision was taken to construct a 300 to 500 MW nuclear power plant. In 1998, steps were taken to construct a 600 MW power plant. The ''nuclear action plan'' was approved in 2000.

In 2005, Bangladesh signed a nuclear cooperation agreement with China. In 2007, the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission (BAEC) proposed two 500 MW nuclear reactors for Rooppur by 2015. In 2008, China offered funding for the project. Instead, the Bangladesh government started discussion with the [[Russia]]n government a year later and on 13 February the two governments signed a [[memorandum of understanding]]. [[Rosatom]] said they would start construction by 2013.<ref>{{cite news |last=Mahbub |first=Sumon |url=http://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2013/01/15/n-plant-funding-deal-cut |title=N-plant funding deal cut |work=bdnews24 |date=15 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.newstoday.com.bd/index.php?option=details&news_id=2334550&date=2013-01-16 |title=PM seeks more Russian investment in ICT sector |work=The News Today |date=15 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.newstoday.com.bd/index.php?option=details&news_id=2334565&date=2013-01-16 |title=Collaboration in defence, telecom agreed upon |work=The News Today |date=15 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-15552687 |title=Bangladesh agrees nuclear power deal with Russia |work=BBC News |date=2 November 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.themoscowtimes.com/news/article/bangladesh-to-get-1bln-loan-for-weapons/474052.html |title=Bangladesh to Get $1Bln Loan for Weapons |work=The Moscow Times |date=16 January 2013}}</ref>

In 2011, [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] conducted ''IAEA Integrated Nuclear Infrastructure Review (INIR)'' mission in Bangladesh. Later on, IAEA approved a technical assistance project for the Rooppur nuclear power plant. In 2013 a group of Bangladeshi scientists and the global diaspora voiced profound concern over the safety and economic viability of the plant.<ref name="VFJ Concern">[http://www.voiceforjustice.org/Nuclear%20Power%20Site%20final.htm], Voice for Justice World Forum, 30 June 2013</ref> Several separate issues were raised, from the unsuitability of the site to the obsolescence of the [[VVER|VVER-1000]] model proposed, questionable financing arrangements and a lack of agreement with Russia over nuclear waste disposal.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://en.prothom-alo.com/bangladesh/news/72915/Rooppur-Plant-reactor-technology-being-changed |title=Rooppur Plant reactor technology being changed |last=Karmaker |first=Arun |date=23 July 2015 |work=[[Prothom Alo]] |access-date=19 July 2016}}</ref>

In 2015, the proposal was delayed by a year. Rosatom offered a two [[VVER-1200]] reactor power plant, increasing output to 2.4 GWe.<ref name="wnn-20151020">{{cite news |url=http://www.neimagazine.com/news/newsdelay-for-bangladesh-nuclear-plant-4698631 |title=Delay for Bangladesh nuclear plant |work=World Nuclear News |date=20 October 2015 |access-date=26 October 2015}}</ref> On December 25, 2015, representatives of the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission and the Russian state nuclear corporation Rosatom signed the contract for the construction of the Rooppur nuclear power plant worth the equivalent of US$12.65 billion.<ref name="DailyStar25Dec2015">{{citation |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/country/rooppur-nuke-plant-1265b-deal-inked-russia-192556 |title=Rooppur nuke plant: $12.65b deal inked with Russia
 |work=The Daily Star |date=25 December 2015}}</ref> Three days later, ''[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]]'' echoed criticism from Germany-based [[Transparency International]] about increased costs, from statements of around US$4 billion made earlier in the same year.<ref name="DailyStar28Dec2015" /> Transparency International also expressed concern about the safety of the proposed plant.<ref name="DailyStar28Dec2015">{{citation |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/country/tib-concerned-over-rooppur-nuke-plants-safety-193483 |title=TIB concerned over Rooppur nuke plant's safety |work=The Daily Star |date=28 December 2015}}</ref>

=== Construction ===
In 2016 ground preparation work commenced.  The $12.65 billion contract is 90% funded by a loan from the Russian government. The two units generating 2.4 GWe are planned to be operational in 2024 and 2025. Rosatom will operate the units for the first year before handing over to Bangladeshi operators. Russia will supply the nuclear fuel and take back [[spent nuclear fuel]].<ref name=nei-20160401>{{cite news |url=http://www.neimagazine.com/news/newscontract-signed-for-preparatory-work-at-bangladeshs-npp-4854452 |title=Contract signed for preparatory work at Bangladesh's NPP |publisher=Nuclear Engineering International |date=1 April 2016 |access-date=4 April 2016}}</ref>

On 4 November 2017, [[Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission]] received, from [[Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority]], the design and construction license of Unit 1, paving the way for the nuclear island first concrete pour.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/backpage/rooppur-gets-design-construction-licence-1486453 |title=Rooppur gets design, construction licence |date=5 November 2017 |work=The Daily Star |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104233051/http://www.thedailystar.net/backpage/rooppur-gets-design-construction-licence-1486453 |archive-date=4 November 2017 |url-status=live |access-date=6 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://energybangla.com/bd-to-pour-first-concrete-for-its-rooppur-npp-on-november-30/ |title=BD To Pour First Concrete For Its Rooppur NPP On November, 30 |date=2 November 2017 |website=energybangla.com |access-date=30 November 2017}}</ref>

The [[nuclear reactor]] and critical infrastructure are being built by [[Russia]]n companies. [[Atomenergomash]] is the engineering division of [[Russia]]'s state nuclear corporation, [[Rosatom]]. This company is the supplier of all the equipment for the [[Nuclear reactor|reactor]] compartment of Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant and a significant part of the equipment for the machine room.<ref name="rosatom.ru"/> Over 70 tenders have been issued for ‘non-critical’ works where [[Bangladesh]]i and [[India]]n construction companies can participate.

On 14 July 2018, the first concrete was poured for Unit 2.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/Articles/Construction-starts-on-second-Bangladeshi-reactor |title=Construction starts on second Bangladeshi reactor |date=16 July 2018 |work=[[World Nuclear News]] |publisher=WNA |access-date=8 August 2018}}</ref> The following month, Rosatom began installing a 200-tonne [[core catcher]] as the first large piece of equipment in the reactor building of Rooppur 1, describing it as "a unique protection system".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.world-nuclear-news.org/Articles/Core-catcher-installation-under-way-at-Rooppur-1 |title=Core catcher installation under way at Rooppur 1 |website=World Nuclear News |access-date=5 June 2019}}</ref>

When the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] struck Bangladesh in early 2020, many projects such as the [[Dhaka Metro Rail]] were stalled, but the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant remained on track to be completed by 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bashar|first=Reazul|title=Rooppur nuclear power plant on 'fast track' despite pandemic|url=https://bdnews24.com/economy/2020/07/12/rooppur-nuclear-power-plant-on-fast-track-despite-pandemic|access-date=2020-07-17|work=bdnews24.com}}</ref> Progress in this period includes [[Rosatom|Rosatom's]] engineering company [[Atommash]] completing hydraulic tests for Rooppur unit 1.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rooppur unit 1 hydraulic tests completed : New Nuclear - World Nuclear News|url=https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/Articles/Rooppur-unit-1-hydraulic-tests-completed|access-date=2020-07-17|website=www.world-nuclear-news.org}}</ref>

== Safety ==
[[VVER|VVER-1200/523]] is one of the latest [[Generation III reactor#First reactors|Generation III+]] nuclear reactor. Design feature of the nuclear reactor is layered safety barriers preventing escape of radioactive material. The reactor has five layers:

# Fuel pellets: Radioactive elements are retained within the crystal structure of the fuel pellets.
# Fuel rods: The zircaloy tubes provide a further barrier resistant to heat and high pressure.
# Reactor shell: a massive steel shell encases the whole fuel assembly [[Hermetic seal|hermetically]].
# Core catcher: A [[core catcher]] is a device provided to catch the molten core material ([[Corium (nuclear reactor)|corium]]) of a nuclear reactor in case of a [[nuclear meltdown]] and prevent it from escaping the containment building.
# Reactor building: A concrete [[containment building]] is the last line of defence. It prevents escape of [[radiation]]. It also protects from external damages.<ref>{{cite web |title=Safety of Rooppur nuclear power plant in Bangladesh ensured at all stages: Experts
|url=https://www.nuclearasia.com/views/safety-rooppur-nuclear-power-plant-bangladesh-ensured-stages-experts/1043/ |website=Nuclear Asia|date=22 September 2017 |access-date=24 Aug 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=VVER-1200 reactors to ensure 5-tier safety at Rooppur nuclear plant
|url=https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/power-energy/2018/01/14/vver-1200-reactors-safety-rooppur-nuclear-plant |work=Dhaka Tribune|access-date=24 Aug 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Five layers of Safety in Nuclear Reactor
|url=http://www.rooppurnpp.gov.bd/site/page/cf844ade-a1f7-4b7c-a9fc-92cbdfb5c3f3/Five-layer-of-Safety---- |website=Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant|access-date=24 Aug 2020}}</ref>

The nuclear part of the plant is housed in a single building acting as containment and missile shield. Besides the reactor and steam generators this includes an improved refueling machine, and the computerized reactor control systems. Likewise protected in the same building are the emergency systems, including an emergency core cooling system, emergency backup diesel power supply, and backup feed water supply. A [[Passive nuclear safety|passive heat removal system]] had been added to the  VVER-1200. The system is based on a cooling system and water tanks built on top of the containment dome.<ref>
{{cite news | title= Passive safety in VVERs | author= V.G. Asmolov | work= JSC Rosenergoatom | publisher= Nuclear Engineering International | date= 26 August 2011 | url= http://www.neimagazine.com/story.asp?storyCode=2060518 | access-date= 6 September 2011 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120319191743/http://www.neimagazine.com/story.asp?storyCode=2060518 | archive-date= 19 March 2012 | url-status= dead | df= dmy-all }}</ref> The passive systems handle all safety functions for 24 hours, and core safety for 72 hours.

Other new safety systems include aircraft crash protection, [[Passive autocatalytic recombiner|hydrogen recombiners]], and a [[core catcher]] to contain the [[Corium (nuclear reactor)|molten reactor core]] in the event of a severe accident. Russia's arms manufacturer Almaz-Antey to install cooling systems for Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant'''.'''<ref>{{Cite web|last=GDC|date=2021-09-13|title=Russian Arms Maker Almaz-Antey Supplies Cooling System For Bangladesh And Turkish Nuclear Power Plant|url=https://www.globaldefensecorp.com/2021/09/14/russian-arms-maker-almaz-antey-supplies-cooling-system-for-bangladesh-and-turkish-nuclear-power-plant/|access-date=2021-09-14|website=Global Defense Corp|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Economics==
The US$12.65 billion project will be constructed with Russian loan amounting US$11.38 billion and the rest will be financed by the Bangladesh government.

With over 90% utilization factor, the power plant is expected to generate 19 billion kWh annually. Levelized Cost of Electricity(LCOE) is 56.73 (USD/MWh) <ref>{{Cite web |title=A snapshot on Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant Project |url=https://rooppurnpp.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/rooppurnpp.portal.gov.bd/notices/7e349f02_ec26_4a27_be29_66ef81041cb8/A%20snapshot%20on%20Rooppur%20Nuclear%20Power%20Plant%20Project.pdf}}</ref>

== Research ==
Bangladesh's development strategy sees the country becoming a middle-income nation by 2021, in large part by emphasis on its science and technology sector to drive economic growth. The ministry of science and technology (MoST) estimated in 2014 that US$6.2 billion will be needed in the next decade to achieve the goals of Vision 2021. The Science and Technology Act 2010 is helping to boost this, and MoST is now allocating over $150 million per year to nuclear technology development as gas reserves become depleted. The power plant will also promote the local economy of Rooppur, Pabna.

The country has had a [[TRIGA]] 3 MW research reactor operational since 1986.<ref>[http://www.world-nuclear.org/information-library/country-profiles/countries-a-f/bangladesh.aspx Nuclear Power in Bangladesh]</ref>
